newsitem.title: USA: Mia Farrow airs bitterness over Woody Allen.
newsitem.headline: Mia Farrow airs bitterness over Woody Allen.

text.p: Actress Mia Farrow, about to publish a scathing memoir of her life with Woody Allen, said in a television interview to be shown on Friday that she does not want to see her adopted daughter, Soon Yi, who is now living with Allen.

"I used to long to see her. I used to cry for her. I couldn't have known her too well. .. maybe she didn't understand what a mother was, what a family was. But I don't think I want to see her anymore," Farrow told ABC-TV's "20/20" news programme.
In an interview with ABC's Barbara Walters, Farrow said she broke with Allen when she discovered that he was having an affair with Soon Yi and found "raunchy" photographs Allen had taken of her.
"I was stunned, it was like an axe fell through me. ... I got to the phone and I called his office and I said, 'I found the pictures. Get away from us.'"

She added that Allen exhibited "rage against women, rage against mothers, against daughters, against families. As a very, very analysed man, he would say there are no accidents. And if that's true, I can think, 'What rage to have left such pictures for a mother to see . .... I thought he was a mortally superior person.'"
Farrow said she tries not to think about Allen today. "I don't spend two seconds thinking about him if I can help it and most of the time I can."
